## Risks the plan misses

**1. The audit-write loss window is the real incident, and the plan doesn't quantify it.** From 2026-08-29 ~11:32 UTC until your hotfix today, every `INSERT` into `platform_audit.audit_events` failed, not just the Alerts-page reads. Depending on how `AuditEventListener` is wired (after-commit listener → events silently dropped; synchronous → business transactions rolled back), you have either a ~1-day hole in a **tamper-evident** platform audit chain or a day of failed operator actions. For a compliance platform under grant-audit scrutiny (your own CLAUDE.md flags exactly this hazard class), "the 500 is fixed" is not closure. Before closing: query the event timestamps around the window to measure the gap, grep app logs for swallowed `permission denied for schema platform_audit` on the write path, and record the window in the ADR-0363 amendment. If the hash chain links prev-hash, a gap doesn't break chain verification — but it must be documented, not discovered by an auditor.

**2. No tripwire — this is the third corrective migration in three days for the same repair, and nothing would catch a fourth.** I read `/Users/robertilisei/Projects/agri-saas-platform/apps/api/src/test/java/ro/agricore/smoke/RolePermissionsIT.java`: it probes *synthetic* roles/tables it creates itself, so it structurally cannot detect prod ACL drift, and nothing anywhere asserts schema-level USAGE post-migrate. The pattern across V202608281000 → V202608291200 → this one is identical: each fix validated only against the symptom just observed (relacl table-wide → relacl per-grantee → nspacl). The catalog has more levels (DB-level CONNECT, default-privilege grantor identity, proacl for future explicit-ACL functions). The actual closing move is a deploy-time assertion: either a health indicator that does a trivial `SELECT` on `platform_audit.audit_events` *as agricore_app* wired into the existing CI health gate (which you just fixed for MailHealthIndicator — the plumbing exists, commit `eef44b9a`), or a terminal verification block in this migration that `RAISE EXCEPTION`s if `has_schema_privilege` is still false after the grant. Without one of these, the migration codifies the fix but not the lesson.

**3. Unverified siblings.** You checked `platform_audit` USAGE but the same implicit-owner-privilege class applies to `public` — almost certainly fine (app is serving traffic, and on PG15+ `public` typically has PUBLIC USAGE), but "no placeholders, no assumptions" is your house rule: run `has_schema_privilege('agricore_app','public','USAGE')` while you're on the box. Also spot-check `has_table_privilege('agricore_backup','platform_audit.audit_events','SELECT')` — V202608291200's per-grantee loop only checked `agricore_app`/`agricore_readonly`, and `agricore_backup` had only schema USAGE in the nspacl you quoted; if its table grants relied on anything implicit, your next backup run of that schema fails silently until restore-test day.

## Alternatives worth considering

- **Drop the `IF NOT has_schema_privilege` guard or keep it knowingly** — `GRANT` is natively idempotent; the guard adds no safety, and it has a mild false-negative: `has_schema_privilege` returns true for privileges inherited via role membership, so in an environment where `agricore_app` inherits USAGE indirectly the direct grant is skipped and the posture diverges from prod. Harmless today; fine to keep for house-pattern consistency, but don't treat it as a correctness feature.
- **Assert the full expected `nspacl` posture in one migration** — since you're codifying prod state anyway, also check-and-grant `agricore_readonly`/`agricore_backup` USAGE (currently present only because `agricore_migrate` granted them manually or via V202608271000-era work). On a fresh rebuild, will those two get platform_audit USAGE from *any* committed migration? If not, dev/staging will drift from prod in the opposite direction.
- **Add the fail-loud verification tail**: after the grant, `IF NOT has_schema_privilege(...) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION` — converts any grantor-privilege edge case into a deploy failure instead of a repeat silent drift.

## Pushback on the weakest points

- **"Could V202608301000 re-break this?" — No, and you could have answered this yourself by reading it.** It's a *tenant*-location, `${schema}`-templated migration (`/Users/robertilisei/Projects/agri-saas-platform/apps/api/src/main/resources/db/migrations/tenant/V202608301000__reanchor_tenant_default_privileges.sql`), runs per `tnt_*` schema in a separate Flyway history, and only touches ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for those schemas. It cannot reach `platform_audit`.
- **"Missing default-privilege anchor for future platform_audit objects?" — already covered, stop worrying about it.** V202608281000 lines 172–173 anchor TABLES (SELECT, INSERT — tamper-evidence posture), V202608291200 lines 112–114 anchor SEQUENCES and FUNCTIONS, all `FOR ROLE agricore_migrate IN SCHEMA platform_audit`. Note one nuance: those anchors fire only for objects *created by* `agricore_migrate` — if `agricore_app` ever creates an object there (it shouldn't, and can't without CREATE), the anchor doesn't apply. Which is another reason your "no CREATE for agricore_app" call is right.
- **The CREATE question — your answer is correct** and consistent with V202608281000's whole threat model (schema-owner cascade-destroy was the thing being *removed* from agricore_app). Granting CREATE back would partially undo ADR-0363.
- **The migration comment says the 500 hit "PlatformAlertsController read" and "AuditEventRepository writes"** — make sure the comment's causal story matches what the logs actually show (schema-level denial, not table-level), since two prior migrations in this series had headers whose stated mental model turned out wrong and had to be corrected by their successors. You verified `has_schema_privilege` false live, so the mechanism is right; just keep the header claims to what you verified.

## Verdict

**Go-with-caveats.** The live hotfix was correct, minimal, and additive; the drafted migration is safe to commit as-is — right guard pattern, right no-op-on-prod convergence behaviour, matches the established V202608291200 idiom, and no interaction with the pending tenant migration. But do not call the incident closed on the migration alone: (1) quantify and document the ~1-day audit-write gap (this is the compliance-relevant part, not the 500), (2) add a deploy-time/health-gate tripwire for `platform_audit` access as agricore_app so the fourth variant of this bug class fails a pipeline instead of a farmer-facing page, (3) spot-check `public` USAGE and `agricore_backup` table grants while you still have the psql session, and (4) amend ADR-0363 to record this second corrective — the ADR's revision history is the only reason you were able to reconstruct this chain at all.
